what_happened: Job 20261030-013721-4gwn (code job: "Give OLY-B-BND-01 a mechanism: refuse writes to any non-origin remote") failed in planning, before any code was written. The critic judged the reading misread the request, and the plan still needed revising at round 3 of 5. The reading contradicts itself: it lists CHANGELOG.md (modify) as a deliverable and carries the changelog default, but criterion 7 requires CHANGELOG.md to be untouched. Admission enforces the changelog default in code, so an admitted candidate cannot meet criterion 7's CHANGELOG clause. Findings: one blocker (leaving CHANGELOG.md untouched gets the candidate refused at admission before the verifier). One major: origin_url uses `git remote get-url --push origin` without `--all`, so it sees only the first push URL, and a second push URL aimed at another repository passes the check. Three minor: crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs is not among the deliverables; no test shows land_pr with no origin does no write; the guard checks the remote's name, not its target. The core design was judged sound. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Nothing cross-checks the reading's acceptance criteria against Athena's defaults and admission rules before planning starts. The changelog default is enforced in code, but the reading wrote a "CHANGELOG.md untouched" criterion next to a CHANGELOG deliverable. The contradiction was only found by the critic, and planning has fixed rounds with no mechanical repair step. The `--all` gap is a separate defect in the plan's own design.
other_causes: The plan relied on git's `get-url --push` output from memory, without checking that it prints only the first URL unless `--all` is given.
The plan's deliverable list was not reconciled with the files it edits (athena-git lib.rs missing from the deliverables).
open_hypotheses: The event shows the verdict at round 3 of 5, but the stored fields do not say whether later rounds ran or why the job ended failed rather than continuing.
Whether the criterion 7 wording came from the request itself or was added by the reader is not shown.
contradictions: The critic's own verdict says the core design is sound and every named file, line and seam checks out, so the failure comes from one reading criterion and one command-flag detail, not a design flaw.
The event says the failure is at round 3 of 5, while a failure in planning normally follows the last round.
prevention: Add a code check run when the reading is accepted, before planning. It compares every criterion that forbids touching a file against the default-required deliverables (CHANGELOG.md from the changelog default) and the admission rules in admission.rs. It rejects or repairs the reading when a criterion would fail correct work. A mechanical contradiction like this would then be caught before any planning round, not by the critic in round 3.
proposed_request:
Add a reading-time check that compares each acceptance criterion with the Athena defaults and admission rules, and refuses or repairs a reading whose criterion contradicts one. First case: a "file X untouched" criterion for CHANGELOG.md while the changelog default is in force and CHANGELOG.md is a deliverable. Acceptance:
- A reading with a "CHANGELOG.md untouched" criterion and the changelog default is flagged before planning starts.
- A reading that lists CHANGELOG.md as a deliverable without such a criterion is not flagged.
- A test replays the check over the readings of past jobs, including 20261030-013721-4gwn, and reports the false-flag count.
- The CHANGELOG.md entry is written.
- fmt, clippy and test pass.
